changes.title: A Day in the Life of a Coal Miner (1910)
changes.from: A rare early‑20th‑century industrial documentary showing the harsh, dangerous, and demanding work of coal miners. Short, raw, and historically valuable, it offers a glimpse into the labor conditions that shaped America’s working class. Rights: Public domain.
changes.to: An early British documentary from Charles Urban's Kineto company, sponsored by the London & North Western Railway. It follows a coal miner through a full working day, from his early-morning goodbyes to the journey home, and shows the women who worked at the pit. Some scenes were staged, because filming underground was not yet possible. Rights: Public domain.
changes.evidence: BFI Screenonline: British Kineto film (Charles Urban), sponsored by the London & North Western Railway; the current text calls it American

changes.title: Elephants Dream (2006)
changes.from: Elephants Dream is the story of two strange characters exploring a capricious and seemingly infinite machine. The elder, Proog, acts as a tour-guide and protector, happily showing off the sights and dangers of the machine to his initially curious but increasingly skeptical protege Emo. As their journey unfolds we discover signs that the machine is not all Proog thinks it is, and his guiding takes on a more desperate aspect. Rights: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 (CC BY 3.0). Credit: Blender Foundation.

changes.title: Sita Sings the Blues (2008)
changes.from: Sita is a goddess separated from her beloved Lord and husband Rama. Nina is an  animator whose husband moves to India, then dumps her by email. Three hilarious shadow puppets narrate both ancient tragedy and modern comedy in this beautifully  animated interpretation of the Indian epic Ramayana. Set to the 1920's jazz vocals of Annette Hanshaw, Sita Sings the Blues earns its tagline as "the Greatest Break-Up Story Ever Told.". Rights: Public domain.
